h1: GinGin Hotel, Trang Old Town — a restored Trang building turned charming central boutique
intro: Trang is full of old shophouses and vintage coffee shops, but well-designed places to stay in the heart of the old town are still rare — GinGin Hotel, Trang Old Town is the answer many travellers were waiting for. It's an old building, carefully restored to keep the original walls and details of the structure, then blended with modern interiors. A small boutique 4-star of about 15 rooms, a 4-minute walk from Trang Railway Station, from approx THB 1,500/night.
galleryAlts: A room at GinGin Hotel with warm tones, keeping parts of the original building wall
A bright room corner by the window, with natural light all day
The hotel restaurant and bar area, with an old-town feel

body.html: GinGin began as an old building on Rama VI Road in the heart of Trang's old town. Instead of tearing it down for a new build, the owners chose to keep the original walls and lines of the structure, then layer modern interiors over them. The result is a hotel with a genuine old-town feel — not a new building dressed up to look old. It's the single thing guests mention most: the way old and new are blended so naturally.

There are only a few room types — Standard King, Standard Twin and a Suite. What guests love is that the rooms are very bright, with lots of windows and natural light all day, especially the corner rooms which are larger and catch light from two sides. Beds are comfortable, the air conditioning is cold, and everything still feels new since the hotel only recently opened. Each room has a flat-screen TV, safe, hairdryer and the usual toiletries.
"Opened the curtains in the morning and light filled the room, with old Trang rooftops outside — it felt like staying in a well-cared-for old house, not an ordinary hotel."

Service is another area that scores consistently high. The team is small but attentive — guests describe it as a warm, personal welcome, genuinely caring, happy to recommend restaurants and things to see around town. Cleanliness draws praise in nearly every review; rooms feel new and tidy. There's a small in-house restaurant and bar for a coffee or an evening drink.

Location is GinGin's trump card. It sits right in the heart of Trang old town, about a 4-minute walk from Trang Railway Station — very handy if you arrive by train. Around it are night markets (Centrepoint / Chinta), morning dim sum spots, vintage coffee shops and local restaurants, all within walking distance. Trang is famous for its food, and from here you can eat your way around all day without ever getting in a car.

Worth knowing before you book: because it's in the middle of the old town beside a road and market, there's some market and traffic noise in the early morning. Light sleepers should ask for a room away from the front road. A few reviews note the shower drains a little slowly, and some wished for a desk in the room. With only about 15 rooms, it fills up fast on long weekends, so book ahead.

The verdict from real guest reviews: GinGin is a great fit for travellers who want to stay in the heart of Trang's old town, walk to sights and food, arrive by train, and like a small, well-designed hotel at a fair price. Standard rooms start from around THB 1,500/night, rising to roughly THB 2,500–2,800 for the Suite in peak periods — good value for a boutique 4-star that still feels brand new in this location.

Just accept that it's a city hotel with no resort facilities, and some city noise in the early morning.

faqTitle: FAQ — GinGin Hotel, Trang Old Town

faq.q: Where is GinGin Hotel in Trang and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 23 Rama VI Road, Thap Thiang, in the heart of Trang's old town · about a 4-minute walk to Trang Railway Station · surrounded by night markets, morning dim sum spots, vintage coffee shops and local restaurants, all walkable · Trang Airport is about a 12-minute drive.

faq.q: How much does GinGin Hotel cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start from around THB 1,500/night for a Standard Twin/King · corner rooms and the Suite run roughly THB 2,100–2,800 · rates vary by season and holidays, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is GinGin Hotel best for?
faq.a: A great fit for travellers who want to stay in the heart of Trang old town, walk to sights and food, arrive by train, and like a small well-designed hotel · it's a city hotel with no pool or resort vibe, so it suits those focused on location and food.

Because it sits beside a road and market in the old town, there's some market and traffic noise in the early morning · light sleepers should ask for a room away from the front road and bring earplugs · outside the early morning it's fairly quiet for a city hotel.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: With only about 15 rooms, long weekends and festivals fill up fast — book 3–4 weeks ahead or more · choose a Free Cancellation rate first if your plans aren't fixed.
